# There is no Denmark

*Generated by `scripts/pages/areas.py` from `data/derived/areas.json`.*

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-AGG">The national argument is made in aggregates: one land-borne load, and one share of it for agriculture - [69.6](SOURCES.md#F-e2cc286a52)% in the figure DANVA cites from Miljøstyrelsen and Aarhus University. Aggregation is where the information goes: a figure true of Denmark need not hold for any one water body inside it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-AGG "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-SCOPE">This page refuses the aggregate. One record per marine water body: what presses on it, what is observed in it, **over which years each of those streams exists**, and what cannot be modelled there.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-SCOPE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ASSIGN">Assignment is by nearest point on the marine boundary, one rule for every layer, with the largest distance kept for each layer in each area and anything beyond [20](SOURCES.md#F-badc2347ae) km dropped.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ASSIGN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What an absence can be counted over

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ABSENCE-RULE">**A claim of absence is only as wide as the search behind it**, and this search was two layers deep.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ABSENCE-RULE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-REGISTER">ODA's station register holds **[6,258](SOURCES.md#F-f2f5d986a1) positioned marine stations**.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-REGISTER "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-SERIES-COVERAGE">The part of it this page can place in water bodies is the station series behind the partition tests below — [1,415](SOURCES.md#F-5fb04be1c0) stations with a monthly record, [1,313](SOURCES.md#F-8a40ae1f65) of them inside a water body by point in polygon — and **[119](SOURCES.md#F-481802d78d) of the [123](SOURCES.md#F-4cb4902088) water bodies contain at least one of those.** Counted over that series: [4](SOURCES.md#F-9552070f3a) water bodies contain no station with data in [2](SOURCES.md#F-3fca6d1b99) or more distinct years, [10](SOURCES.md#F-335ad5024c) water bodies contain no station with data in [5](SOURCES.md#F-4549390408) or more distinct years, [12](SOURCES.md#F-4ad752eb92) water bodies contain no station with data in [10](SOURCES.md#F-e17184bafe) or more distinct years.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-SERIES-COVERAGE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-NOT-PERCENT">**Those are counts, and they are deliberately not percentages.** Saying *[8](SOURCES.md#F-f02c7ae231)% of the sea has no long observation* would be the missing-denominator error this project exists to point at. The denominator is known — the sea is [43,579](SOURCES.md#F-655cb351e2) km². The numerator is not, because it is the extent of an absence, and an absence can only be measured against a search that was exhaustive. Ours was ODA plus two layers; ICES and EMODnet sit outside it, and so does whatever university, municipal or unpublished series exist.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-NOT-PERCENT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

The test is whether **the category named is the same width as the corpus searched.**

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-SAME-WIDTH">**Same width — an exact statement is fine, including of an absence.** *None of the [123](SOURCES.md#F-2f37b30ded) water bodies has a marine point in the national hazardous-substance layer: its [256](SOURCES.md#F-9edac16b2c) points are [152](SOURCES.md#F-076f9f4115) lake and [104](SOURCES.md#F-0b7a823dec) river.* The category is that layer and the count is of all of it, so its complement is exact.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-SAME-WIDTH "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-WIDER">**Category wider than corpus — only a count is honest.** *[56](SOURCES.md#F-e1ba4b224c)% of the sea has no marine observation* would name a category — marine observation — far wider than the two layers actually searched, and report the leftover after subtracting what we happened to find as though it were measured, which is the operation [RESIDUAL.md](RESIDUAL.md) is about.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-WIDER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-NAMED-CORPUS">So absence is reported here as a count over a named corpus, and the corpus is named every time.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-NAMED-CORPUS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-GAPS">**And the corpus is named together with what is missing from it.** A coverage figure has a numerator nobody can measure — the evidence that exists — so counting what we assembled gives a *lower bound on evidence* and therefore an *upper bound on absence*. That is only interpretable beside the terms we know belong in the numerator and cannot add. They are kept in `data/manual/coverage_gaps.json`, a hand-kept record, in three kinds:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-GAPS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

| | source | what it would add | why we do not have it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `closed` | **PULS** | The time axis for [B1](hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow") and [B2](HYPOTHESES.md "Separate stormwater"). Their discriminating test is oxygen and shore condition in the days after an overflow against that event's volume, which an annual total cannot do. | CVR-gated. Not merely a login: an access attempt with a private MitID was refused on the grounds that no CVR or VAT number attached to it was valid. Access appears to require a registered business or authority entity, so a private citizen cannot obtain it at all. |
| `closed` | **LER** | The drainage network itself, which open problem `16` says exists for exactly one Danish city and only by lucky archaeology. | Not open data. This project does not query it and no argument here depends on it. |
| `open_unassembled` | **MUNICIPAL-SPILDEVANDSPLANER** | Real catchment boundaries, which are the hard test for the inference method in X21. | None. Nobody has assembled them. Some are already in data/raw/plan_html/. |
| `open_unassembled` | **ICES-EMODNET** | Marine observation outside ODA entirely, including the cross-border series that a national extract cannot contain. | Free registration, not completed. |
| `absent` | **FISH-KILL-REGISTER** | The observable behind fiskedoed, one of the four words the public uses for the damage. | Checked and not found in open form. The surveillance is described publicly; no database is linked. |
| `closed` | **MECHANISTIC-MODEL-RUNS** | The ability to check the validation claims in GRUNDLAGET.md directly rather than through their authors' description of them. | Not published as data. The method reports are public; the runs are not. |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-GAP-CLASSES">The distinction inside that table matters as much as the table. `closed` is a gap in the world's availability; `open_unassembled` is a gap in our effort and is nobody's fault but ours; `absent` is the only one where a search was run to the end, and even that is bounded by the search.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-GAP-CLASSES "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-PULS">**PULS is the sharpest case.** It holds the per-event overflow volumes that [B1](hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow") calls the single most valuable missing series — volumes that are themselves largely modelled, by this project's source register — and an access attempt with a private MitID was refused because no CVR or VAT number attached to it was valid, so this is not a login anyone has neglected to perform. Access appears to require a registered business or authority, in which case a private citizen cannot obtain it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-PULS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Two meanings of "a body of water", and the switch between them

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ENCLOSURE">"Roskilde Fjord" is not an arbitrary line on a map, and it is worth saying so plainly before objecting to anything. It names a real hydrographic object: an inlet bounded by land that opens to the sea through Isefjorden. That is a **claim about enclosure**, it is physical, and it is true.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ENCLOSURE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-HOMOGENEITY">The assessment then uses the same word to mean something else entirely: that a measurement taken anywhere in it stands for the whole of it. That is a **claim about homogeneity**, and it is statistical. One sense is about where the water is bounded; the other is about whether the water inside those bounds is alike. Nothing carries you from the first to the second, and the name does the carrying unnoticed because the same three words serve both.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-HOMOGENEITY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-PHYSICS">**And where exchange is restricted, the physics runs against the transfer, not with it.** Restricted exchange is what *preserves* a gradient. A basin with freshwater entering at its head and little exchange at its mouth holds salinity, residence-time and oxygen gradients along its length because it does not flush; open water erases such differences by mixing. So the better the enclosure, the weaker the homogeneity assumption becomes: the two senses **pull in opposite directions**, and the enclosures that most deserve their names are the ones least entitled to be treated as single units.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-PHYSICS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-TWO-UNITS">The partition half-concedes this without following it through. Roskilde Fjord appears here as two water bodies, `DKCOAST1` (ydre, [71](SOURCES.md#F-1e2174d480) km²) and `DKCOAST2` (indre, [52](SOURCES.md#F-721904d9f2) km²) — an admission that one enclosure is at least two units.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-TWO-UNITS "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-SPLIT-UNSTATED">The documents this project holds give the general basis for water bodies' boundaries — the water framework directive asks member states to set them, and the plans sort coastal waters into types with a catchment each — but none of them says why this fjord is two units rather than one or three, or what measurement would settle it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-SPLIT-UNSTATED "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-X22">A boundary drawn inside a fjord is a hypothesis about where the water changes, and it can be tested: `X22` in [EXPERIMENTS.md](EXPERIMENTS.md) sets out how, using pairs of measurements at matched separation either side of a line.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-X22 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-POSITION">The practical rule that follows, and the reason the station-level series exist: **the unit of observation is a position.** Everything else — this page included — is an aggregate computed inside somebody's polygon, and should be read as a statement about that polygon as much as about the sea.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-POSITION "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### The switch, measured in the fjord it is named after

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ROSK-METHOD">The station-level series make this checkable rather than arguable. Both halves of Roskilde Fjord carry several stations, so for any month where [3](SOURCES.md#F-47737412fa) or more measured, the disagreement *between* stations can be set against the variation *across* months. *Spread between stations* is the population standard deviation across the stations in a month, averaged over the months, beside the median range; *spread across months* is the standard deviation of the monthly means.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ROSK-METHOD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ILTSVIND">In Denmark, oxygen below [4](SOURCES.md#F-6f707414ef) mg/L is called iltsvind.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ILTSVIND "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ROSK-OXY">**The inner fjord's own stations disagree about bottom oxygen by a median of [3.35](SOURCES.md#F-9f772be675) mg/l within a single month.** A spread that size is most of the distance from zero to that threshold, so in a month when the fjord's bottom water is near it, one station can read below and another above — and whether that body "has iltsvind" can then depend on which of its own stations is read. The ratio puts it another way: the spread between stations is **[65](SOURCES.md#F-fd09d07246)% of the spread of the monthly means across months**.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ROSK-OXY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ROSK-HALVES">**And the two halves fail on different variables.** The inner fjord's stations disagree for oxygen ([0.65](SOURCES.md#F-fbcf0ce589)) and agree for salinity ([0.29](SOURCES.md#F-791801daea)); the outer fjord's are the reverse — close for oxygen ([0.25](SOURCES.md#F-3c4eacfb1c)), apart for salinity ([0.87](SOURCES.md#F-934bf566cd)). ## What are the baskets predictive FOR? — and how easily that question is answered wrongly

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-PART-STAT">A partition is not right or wrong in general; it is predictive *for a variable*. So the question is what the water bodies encode. The statistic, computed within month by `scripts/partition_score.py`, is a **ratio of mean squares**: the between-basket mean square over the sum of the between- and within-basket mean squares. One means stations in the same basket agree completely. With labels that carry no information both mean squares estimate the same variance and the ratio sits near one half, not zero — so no value in the table below can be read on its own, only its difference from a null.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-PART-STAT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-WITHIN-MONTH">Within month is essential. Every station in Denmark shares a season, so pooling across months puts the seasonal signal into the between-basket term and makes every partition look excellent, including an absurd one.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-WITHIN-MONTH "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-THREE-RANKINGS">**The result depends almost entirely on what it is compared against, and three reasonable comparisons give three different rankings.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-THREE-RANKINGS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

| surface oxygen saturation | [0.924](SOURCES.md#F-84e0d969dc) | [0.859](SOURCES.md#F-16c2345f41) | [0.516](SOURCES.md#F-69ef770902) | [0.522](SOURCES.md#F-79ea3f3d8b) | **[+0.402](SOURCES.md#F-07a23e44f0)** | [0.178](SOURCES.md#F-367e7923a3) |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-NULLS">The three nulls answer three different questions. **Shuffled** permutes station labels while keeping basket sizes, so it destroys geography and keeps the size structure. **Latitude stripes** are equal-count horizontal bands, as many as there are real baskets, so they keep compactness and equal sizes but ignore hydrography. **Size- and shape-matched** baskets have the same size distribution as the real ones and are grown from random seeds by nearest neighbour, three times over, so they are compact blobs of the right sizes following no hydrography at all — the only control that varies one thing at a time.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-NULLS "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-WINNERS">Against the shuffle, salinity gains most, by a distance; against the stripes, surface oxygen saturation does.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-WINNERS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-REVERSAL">Against the matched blobs the ordering **reverses**: surface oxygen saturation gains most ([+0.402](SOURCES.md#F-07a23e44f0)), surface salinity little ([+0.124](SOURCES.md#F-e6d5c2a74c)), and fluorescence's lift is below zero ([-0.050](SOURCES.md#F-db2387434e)) — but the three blob runs themselves spread by [0.109](SOURCES.md#F-ff5c44079f) for fluorescence, so for it the official partition does no better than random compact blobs, and whether it does worse is not shown.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-REVERSAL "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-READING">One reading fits these numbers, and it is not tested here: if salinity is spatially smooth, any compact grouping predicts it well ([0.844](SOURCES.md#F-885a40a1da) from random blobs) and the real boundaries have little left to add; if oxygen is spatially rough, blobs do poorly and boundaries that follow enclosure carry real information.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-READING "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-LIFT-RULE">A partition's value is not how well it predicts, but **how much better it predicts than its own shape alone would**.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-LIFT-RULE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-SAMPLED">One further limit bounding every row: stations are not placed at random and are far denser in some baskets than others, so this scores the partition *as sampled*. It cannot distinguish a well-drawn basket from one whose stations happen to sit close together.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-SAMPLED "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The cum hoc estimate, across areas instead of across years

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-CUMHOC">A national time series has one unit of replication. The water bodies with two or more bathing stations number [65](SOURCES.md#F-d528968118), so an effect size can be estimated across them.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-CUMHOC "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-CUMHOC-DESIGN">This sets bathing-water quality against sewage pressure — outfall, treatment-plant and basin density per km² — because both sides of that pair exist per area. It is **cum hoc**: a correlation across places at one time, with no control for coast type, flushing, or population.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-CUMHOC-DESIGN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

| predictor | outcome | r | $R^2$ | areas |

| `log10(1+outfalls_per_km2)` | mean_score | [-0.136](SOURCES.md#F-24c05f444c) | [0.019](SOURCES.md#F-693b29e24c) | [65](SOURCES.md#F-8253263535) |
| `log10(1+pe_per_km2)` | sub_excellent | [+0.313](SOURCES.md#F-00f9f19776) | [0.098](SOURCES.md#F-f69837d6e1) | [65](SOURCES.md#F-4ea7f73896) |
| `log10(1+pe_per_km2)` | mean_score | [-0.288](SOURCES.md#F-28bf1f6f27) | [0.083](SOURCES.md#F-e25ec24bc4) | [65](SOURCES.md#F-5c4f399df5) |
| `log10(1+basin_m3_per_km2)` | sub_excellent | [+0.139](SOURCES.md#F-a4495c34ea) | [0.019](SOURCES.md#F-7407ebe8ef) | [65](SOURCES.md#F-1988d87992) |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-RECORD">The full record for each area — every pressure, every stream with its years, and the written-out list of what cannot be modelled there — is in `data/derived/areas.json`, which `scripts/areas.py` writes locally and the repository does not ship, and drawn with its timeline on [the map](areas.html).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-RECORD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What this is not

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-NOT">It is not a causal model per area. It is the ledger you need before you can build one: which areas have enough observation to support a claim, which have none, and over which years each stream exists — so that an analysis published in 2025 cannot quietly rest on a relation fitted to 1990–2012 without a reader seeing the gap.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-NOT "What this claim rests on")</sup>
